# Twitter (X.com) Scraper Unlimited: No Limits

The Apify actor [`apidojo/twitter-scraper-lite`](https://apify.com/apidojo/twitter-scraper-lite) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its default build **0.0.1052** (module version **0.1.0**). Runs use whatever build the actor has as default when they start, so they keep working as Apify retires old builds; the input types below are refreshed weekly and can lag an actor that changed its input since.

Introducing Twitter Scraper Unlimited, the most comprehensive Twitter data extraction solution available. Our enterprise-grade scraper offers unmatched capabilities with a transparent event-based pricing model, making it perfect for both small-scale and large-scale data extraction needs.

## Pricing

Pay per event — Search/Profile/List etc Query $0.016, Single Tweet URL Query $0.05, Dataset Item Tier 1 $0.0004, Dataset Item Tier 2 $0.0008, Dataset Item Tier 3 $0.0012, Dataset Item Tier 4 $0.0016, Dataset Item Tier 5 $0.002 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apidojo/twitter-scraper-lite) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apidojo-twitter-scraper-lite@0.1.0#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `searchTerms` | array |  |  | What search terms do you want to scrape? — If you add search terms, the scraper will find and extract tweets that mention those terms. Alternatively, see further down to scrape by Twitter URL. |
| `sort` | string |  |  | Do you want to filter by content? — Sorts search results. If you are getting low results, try Top instead of Latest. Latest + Top runs both simultaneously to maximize results but may return some duplicate tweets. |
| `maxItems` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of tweets — This value lets you set the maximum number of tweets to retrieve. Twitter has a default limit of around 800 tweets per query. Check the README for workarounds. |
| `start` | string |  |  | Tweets from this date — Scrape tweets starting from this date |
| `end` | string |  |  | Tweets until this date — Scrape tweets until this date |
| `twitterHandles` | array |  |  | Do you want to scrape by Twitter handle? — You can add the twitter handles of specific profiles you want to scrape. This is a shortcut so that you don't have to add full username URLs like https://twitter.com/apify |
| `startUrls` | array |  |  | Do you want to scrape by Twitter URL? — This lets you tell the scraper where to start. You can enter Twitter URLs one by one. You can also link to or upload a text file with a list of URLs |
| `includeSearchTerms` | boolean |  |  | Include Search Terms — If selected, a field will be added to each tweets about the search term that was used to find it. |
| `outputConnector` | string |  |  | Send results to Notion, Todoist, … (optional) — Pick an MCP connector you authorized in Console → Settings → API & Integrations → MCP connectors (e.g. Notion, Todoist — any service whose MCP server offers non-destructive write tools works best-effort). The scraped results are written through your ow |
| `deliverTarget` | string |  |  | Destination target — Where to write into the connector — paste the URL or ID. Notion example: https://www.notion.so/My-Posts-24f8a1b2c3d44e5f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b. Leave empty for services that need no target (e.g. Todoist Inbox, Slack). For Notion, share the page or database with your connector first (N |
| `deliverMode` | string |  | `"perPost"` | Write mode — perPost writes one record per scraped item; summary writes a single roll-up for the run. |
| `deliverMaxItems` | integer |  |  | Max records to deliver — perPost only (optional) — Cap on how many records perPost mode writes to the connector; ignored in summary mode. Leave empty to deliver everything scraped. |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
